title: Crestline Energy - Procurement: MSA & DPA Review
summary: Procurement-focused call to review MSA/DPA redlines, discuss SLA tiers and pricing approvals for a Dedicated vs Hosted deployment. Redwood AE and SE walked through security pack, BYOK options, and onboarding steps. Customer legal and procurement requested redline, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and pricing details for internal approvals; next steps and action items agreed.
next_steps: Jenna to send MSA redline with track changes by 2026-09-02
Marcus to share SOC2 & ISO packages and network diagram by 2026-09-03
Provide pricing deck with committed capacity & SLA tiers by 2026-09-02
Customer to open vendor profile in procurement portal and route PO path
action_items: Jenna Park: Send MSA redline + pricing options (tracked changes) - due 2026-09-02
Marcus Li: Share security pack (SOC2 report, ISO docs, architecture diagram) - due 2026-09-03
Meera Patel / Ravi Shah: Confirm required audit log retention and KMS policy for BYOK - due 2026-09-04
Daniel Price: Send Crestline standard redline template (if any) - due 2026-09-01
transcript: 00:00:00 Jenna Park: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. We, we really appreciate you making time. I'm Jenna, AE on the account. Marcus is our SE and Tina from success is on to cover onboarding. 00:00:18 Laura Gomez: Thanks Jenna. We have legal and procurement on the line, wanted to get through MSA and DPA redlines and confirm SLAs and pricing so our approvers can sign off. 00:00:29 Daniel Price: Hi all, Daniel here, I'll be leading the legal review. Quick heads up, we generally push on indemnity and liability caps, also data residency and deletion obligations. 00:00:40 Marcus Li: Great, thanks Daniel. We'll try to call out where Redwood is flexible. Quick clarifier, when you say data residency, do you mean in-region processing for PII or longer-term storage restrictions? 00:00:52 Ravi Shah: Mostly processing region, and the DPA needs to list retention periods and who controls KMS keys. We're evaluating hosted API vs dedicated capacity and worried about keys. 00:01:05 Jenna Park: Understood. To frame the options: Hosted Redwood API is fastest to go live, usage-based billing. Redwood Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and isolation; Redwood Private is the VPC/on-prem option for full control and BYOK. 00:01:22 Laura Gomez: Cost is a big factor - procurement wants committed spend options. We'll need pricing tiers for committed capacity and overage rules. Also SLA levels - 99.9 vs 99.95 - and what credits look like. 00:01:35 Marcus Li: For SLAs we offer standard and premium SLOs; credits are tiered, and for Dedicated we can look at tighter latency targets. We'll include explicit MTTF/MTTR language in the SLA doc. 00:01:47 Daniel Price: On the MSA text, two things: one, can we get a mutual NDA and third-party subprocessors listed in the DPA? Two, limitation of liability - Crestline typically pushes for higher caps for security breaches. 00:02:02 Jenna Park: We usually have a standard liability cap tied to fees, but we can discuss higher limits on enterprise plans - that's something I'll flag with contracts. Also we maintain a subprocessor list and can provide SOC2 details. 00:02:18 Meera Patel: Can you confirm encryption in transit and at rest, and whether we can use our KMS/HSM? We require BYOK for keys used for PII. 00:02:30 Marcus Li: Yes, encryption in transit and at rest by default. For Redwood Private and some Dedicated options we support BYOK - you can integrate your KMS/HSM. For hosted we offer bring-your-own-key in certain enterprise plans; we'll send the integration guidance. 00:02:48 Laura Gomez: OK, good. On deletion: the DPA needs explicit delete-by dates and certification that backups are purged within X days. We have internal auditors who will validate. 00:02:59 Marcus Li: We'll include retention and purge windows in the DPA. Note that for caching and KV cache behavior, live inference caches might persist short-lived prefixes - we can add explicit language about cache expiry. 00:03:15 Daniel Price: Also want to understand logs and audit trails - we need per-request audit logs for 12 months and controls around access. 00:03:24 Marcus Li: Redwood Console provides token-level traces and per-route dashboards; audit logs are available with enterprise retention options. We'll include examples of log fields and retention SLAs. 00:03:36 Jenna Park: If useful, we'll attach a sample security pack and network diagram after the call. Link: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (note: link for reference). 00:03:45 Meera Patel: Great. Another procurement note: we have an internal vendor risk questionnaire - can you fill that, and do you have cyber insurance details? 00:03:56 Jenna Park: Yes, we'll fill the vendor questionnaire and share insurance certs. 00:04:02 Laura Gomez: Pricing approvals - our finance team needs a one-page TCO with committed vs on-demand numbers, and delta for Dedicated. 00:04:12 Marcus Li: We'll prepare a pricing deck with committed capacity scenarios, overage rules, and expected per-token costs with and without cache/batching. We'll call out model quantization and batching savings that Redwood Optimize suggests. 00:04:25 Daniel Price: On termination/exit clauses - we need clear data export timelines and a sandbox copy for data migration. 00:04:33 Jenna Park: We can include export windows and a migration playbook; for Dedicated or Private we'll support a full export API and assistance. 00:04:41 Ravi Shah: From a technical perspective, for Dedicated we need vpc peering and private endpoints; can we get a network diagram and expected ports? 00:04:50 Marcus Li: Yes, we'll provide network diagrams, port lists, and firewall rules. For Dedicated we can support VPC peering or private link depending on your cloud. 00:05:02 Daniel Price: Any mandatory audit rights? Our compliance team usually asks to run periodic scans. 00:05:08 Jenna Park: We provide audit logs and SOC2; active scans we typically coordinate with security and sign an arrangement. We'll surface the policy in the security pack. 00:05:18 Laura Gomez: Timeline - procurement needs vendor approval by mid-September. We have a pricing committee meeting on 2026-09-08. 00:05:27 Jenna Park: Noted. We'll aim to have redlines and pricing docs to you by 2026-09-02 so you can route. 00:05:34 Meera Patel: A couple of clarifying Qs: Are there any data residency guarantees for hosted? And what about fallbacks - if a region is down does traffic reroute and where is the data processed? 00:05:44 Marcus Li: For hosted we offer region pinning for data processing, but full residency guarantees are on Private deployments. For regional failover, we route by policy - fallback may process in a nearby compliant region unless you opt out. We'll document the routing and fallback policy. 00:06:02 Daniel Price: Also want to confirm subcontractor list - Atlassian? Kubernetes providers? 00:06:08 Jenna Park: Our subprocessor list includes major cloud providers; we'll provide the current list. 00:06:15 Laura Gomez: Ok good. Procurement process: once we have redline and security artifacts we'll go through legal and procurement approval; we may require a PO and insurance addendum. 00:06:25 Jenna Park: Totally. We also have an onboarding checklist - Tina can walk through technical onboarding requirements and timeline. 00:06:31 Tina Morales: Hi all, onboarding typically takes 2-4 weeks for hosted, 6-10 weeks for Dedicated depending on peering and cert approvals. We'll add milestone dates once pilot scope is defined. 00:06:45 Ravi Shah: For the pilot we'd like to run a small production-like workload to benchmark latency and cost. Can we get a trial cluster or test endpoint? 00:06:55 Marcus Li: Yes, we can spin up a pilot Dedicated slice or provide hosted trial credits. We'll gather expected qps, sequence lengths, and model variant to size the pilot. 00:07:08 Laura Gomez: On pricing, a question - do you offer enterprise discounts if we commit annually? Our procurement prefers annual committed spend. 00:07:16 Jenna Park: Yes, reserved capacity contracts are monthly/annual commits. Discounts scale with commit levels; we'll provide sample tiers. 00:07:24 Daniel Price: Back to MSA - indemnity and breach notification windows. We need 72-hour notification for incidents and a breach playbook. 00:07:33 Jenna Park: We have standard incident response SLAs; 72-hour notification is consistent with our policies, we'll include an incident playbook. 00:07:41 Meera Patel: For BYOK, what KMS integrations do you support? We use [redacted] HSM and AWS KMS. 00:07:49 Marcus Li: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and external HSM via PKCS#11 in Private deployments. We'll include integration docs. 00:08:00 Daniel Price: One common procurement hold up is insurance. What's your cyber liability and umbrella insurance limits? 00:08:07 Jenna Park: We'll share current insurance certificates; typically we carry cyber liab limits that align with enterprise contracts, we can surface specifics in the security pack. 00:08:15 Laura Gomez: Sounds good. Any notes on benchmarking? We need an apples-to-apples latency/cost spreadsheet for our infra team. 00:08:22 Marcus Li: We'll attach our benchmark spreadsheet and can run a custom benchmark for your workload as part of pilot. Note that throughput, sequence length, and KV cache usage materially affect cost. 00:08:35 Ravi Shah: Please document assumptions around quantization and model variants - some model variants may be cheaper but affect quality. 00:08:42 Marcus Li: Absolutely, we'll highlight model/quantization tradeoffs in the pricing doc. 00:08:48 Daniel Price: Any competitors we should be aware of in your references? Procurement sometimes calls them out. 00:08:54 Jenna Park: Customers evaluate a mix of managed LLM APIs and self-hosted runtimes; we'll provide competitive differentiation notes. 00:09:02 Laura Gomez: Great. Logistics: handoffs - once legal gets redline we'll try to respond within 3 business days, procurement wants pricing deck and TCO. 00:09:12 Jenna Park: We will aim for the 2026-09-02 deliverables then. 00:09:17 Tina Morales: For onboarding, please prepare SSO/SAML details and RBAC requirements - we support SAML/Okta and SCIM for provisioning. 00:09:27 Meera Patel: We use Okta; SCIM provisioning is preferred. 00:09:31 Marcus Li: Noted, we'll include SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints. 00:09:38 Daniel Price: A final ask from legal: we need to see prior SOC2 report redacted and retention details. 00:09:44 Jenna Park: We'll share the SOC2 report via secure link and include retention details in the security pack. 00:09:51 Laura Gomez: OK let's recap next steps. 00:09:54 Jenna Park: Recap: we'll send MSA redline + pricing by 2026-09-02, Marcus will send security artifacts by 2026-09-03, and we'll schedule a pilot kickoff tentatively 2026-09-07. Customer will open vendor profile and share redline template by 2026-09-01. 00:10:14 Daniel Price: Sounds good, we'll try to review quickly. 00:10:18 Jenna Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by email with links and attachments. 00:10:22 Laura Gomez: Thanks, talk soon. 00:10:25 [meeting ends]
